thread:
Maya: Heads up — after the BIOS/BMC microcode push to eu-west1 last night we're seeing ~20 GPU nodes stuck in PROVISIONING. PXE times out and OOB logs show eth0 flaps on the BMC side.
Sunil: Can you paste the BMC syslog snippet? guessing link negotiation (QSFP) or NIC firmware mismatch.
Maya: sure, here's the relevant tail from one node's OOB:
```
Mar 17 02:13:44 bmc kernel: eth0: link down (autoneg failure)
Mar 17 02:13:46 bmc kernel: eth0: link up - 10Gbps Full
Mar 17 02:13:47 bmc kernel: eth0: link down (SFP TX disable)
Mar 17 02:13:49 bmc dhcpd: PXE: client timeout
Mar 17 02:13:50 bmc securebootd: SBT flag toggled -> enabled (commit id: cb1f3)
```
Liam: interesting — log shows a secure-boot toggle right after the link flap. I think the BIOS flash may have set lockdown (SBT) on a subset of SKUs which causes the BMC to reset networking stack during SEL changes.
Maya: Confirmed: about 6 nodes had SBT flipped to enabled unexpectedly. Those nodes also show repeated BMC reboots in last 30m.
Nora: Qs: are these identical hardware revs? If QSFP negotiation is unhappy it could hit link training loops and wake a watchdog path in the BMC.
Sunil: yes same build, but two different NIC firmware bundles. After the BIOS change the PHY driver starts renegotiating aggressively.
infra-bot: BIOS-roll/2026-03-17 completed on eu-west1 (nodes: gpu-eu-10..gpu-eu-40), artifact: bios-v4.2.1, runbook: rdw-oob-bios-roll
Liam: Proposed immediate actions:
- Abort further rollout in eu-west1 (pause job) :eyes:
- Canary rollback of bios-v4.2.0 on 2 affected nodes
- Force bring up MDF provisioning via serial PXE over oob on canary
- Open vendor ticket for QSFP negotiation regression
Maya: Paused the rollout (job id: roll-eu-bios-321). Moving remaining hosts out of rotation for safety.
Nora: I'll take the canary rollback and validate NIC firmware interplay. Starting with gpu-eu-12 and gpu-eu-19. ETA 25m.
Sunil: If canary looks good, suggest we do a staged rollback of the rest in 5-node batches. Also we should disable automatic SBT commits in the flash script until vendor confirms.
Maya: Agreed. Also bumping capacity request to us-west1 by 30 GPUs to handle immediate provisioning load — expect cost spike, will alert finance.
Liam: Workaround note for on-call: if PXE times out, use serial-console -> run `ip link set eth0 up` then `dhclient eth0` on BMC to kick negotiation, then trigger reprovision. Add this to runbook.
Nora: Canary rollback done on gpu-eu-12, gpu-eu-19. Post-rollback logs look stable, no eth0 flaps for 12m. PXE succeeded on both.
Maya: Great. Rolling rollback for next batch (gpu-eu-20..24). Please update the runbook: disable SBT auto-commit and add serial workaround.
Sunil: Opening vendor ticket now: TKT-14287 -> subject: "QSFP autoneg regression after BIOS v4.2.1". attaching syslogs and commit id. cc: hw-plat-team.
Liam: I'll monitor provisioning queues and start failover to us-west capacity if we see queue > 40 pending.
Maya: Thanks all. Postmortem note: don't run the SBT commit step in mass until vendor confirms. Follow-up actions: vendor triage, runbook update, cost notice to finance, full rollback schedule if vendor can't patch within 24h.
Nora: Will send a short thread to #incidents and ping sales for impacted customers. :thumbsup:
Maya: status update at +2h or when rollback finishes. :white_check_mark:
